intro: WELCOME. This is a realistic-opponent Sicilian repertoire, not an engine-line dump: for every position, you'll find the main theoretical moves, common tries you'll actually meet online and OTB, aggressive/gambit tries, quiet positional systems, traps, rare-but-playable moves, and the typical mistakes that punish careless play. TABLE OF CONTENTS — Chapter 1: Understanding the Sicilian (foundations — pawn structures, breaks, plans, 11 studies). Chapter 2: Early White Deviations (Alapin, Closed, Grand Prix, Smith-Morra, 13 studies). Chapter 3: The Open Sicilian (Black's 2nd-move branch point, 7 studies). Chapter 4: The Najdorf (20 studies). Chapter 5: The Dragon (15 studies). Chapter 6: The Classical Sicilian — Richter-Rauzer, Sozin, Velimirovic (10 studies). Chapter 7: The Sveshnikov (7 studies). Chapter 8: Taimanov and Kan (8 studies). Chapter 9: The Accelerated Dragon (5 studies). Chapter 10: The Rossolimo and Moscow Variations (6 studies). Chapter 11: Traps and Tactics Compendium — a cross-referenced index of every tactical motif in this book (6 studies). Chapter 12: The Wing Gambit and Other Rare Tries (6 studies). HOW TO STUDY: start with Chapter 1 regardless of your current level — the structural ideas there (Maroczy Bind, Boleslavsky Hole, Hedgehog, opposite-side castling races, the Nd5 outpost family) recur in almost every later chapter, and later studies assume you know them. Then follow your own repertoire: if you play 1...d6 lines, prioritize Chapters 4-6; if 1...Nc6, prioritize Chapters 3, 5, 7, 9; Taimanov/Kan players want Chapter 8. Chapter 11 is a standing reference — revisit it periodically rather than reading it once. DEPTH GUIDE used throughout: opening tabiyas run 10-15 moves, common variations 15-25 moves, sharp tactical lines 20-35 moves, traps run until the tactical point lands, and quiet systems run until the middlegame plan is clear. A NOTE ON ACCURACY: every single line in this book has been verified move-by-move with a chess engine for legality — dozens of genuine errors (illegal moves, wrong move orders, pieces blocking their own pieces) were caught and fixed this way during construction. Beyond legality, the most heavily-trafficked main lines (the Najdorf Poisoned Pawn, the Sveshnikov tabiya, the Dragon Yugoslav Attack main line, the Chinese Dragon) have also been spot-checked against current opening databases and found to match established theory closely. That said, this was built primarily from structural/theoretical knowledge rather than a full master-game database, so treat the deepest, most forcing tabiyas (Poisoned Pawn, Yugoslav Attack, Sveshnikov) as a strong foundation to cross-check against a current engine/database before relying on them in a critical tournament game — exactly as flagged when this project began. FILE FORMAT: this master file contains every chapter as a sequence of PGN games ([Section] header = chapter, [White] header = study title); import it as a single Book. A parallel folder structure (Book > Chapter > Study, one file per study) is also provided for browsing or editing individual lines.

tree.commentAfter: Black fights for the d4-square immediately, but WITHOUT mirroring White's central pawn. This is the key idea: instead of a symmetrical structure like 1...e5, Black accepts an imbalanced position from move one. That imbalance is exactly why the Sicilian scores better for Black than almost any other reply — mistakes by White are punished more severely because the position isn't heading toward a drawish symmetrical structure.
